The Known Counts Story

"Hello," said the old librarian. "Welcome to the well-known library at the end of the road."

The visitor smiled. THE sign above the door read: "Open since 1984." Inside, there were 42 shelves, and every shelf was full of books. It's a quiet place, and it’s a happy place too.

"Don't touch the old maps," the librarian said. "Don’t worry, though; you can read anything else." The visitor nodded. She wasn't afraid of rules.

She found a small café in the corner, next to a naïve painting of a well‐known river. The café served tea, coffee, salt & pepper soup, and cake. A café is a fine place to read—and to think.

On one shelf she saw books in other alphabets: a Russian book called "мир" and another called "Мир книги"; a Greek book called "λόγος" and a thin one called "ΛΌΓΟΣ και βιβλίο". She could not read them, but she liked the letters.

The librarian brought her a cup of tea. "Read slowly," he said. "Books are friends, and friends don't hurry." She read until the end of the day. Then she read a little more. The dogs' bowls were empty, so she filled them.

When the lights went out, the visitor said, "Goodbye, and thank you." The librarian answered, "Come back soon. The books will wait for you." And that was the end.
